notes: Line-based heuristics. Every match is a SUSPECTED issue until the agent traces the data flow (see references/methodology.md). Fields: languages = extension groups defined in scripts/nfaudit/util.py; requires = regex that must appear somewhere in the file; unless = regex that, if present on the matched line, discards the match; unless_file = regex that, if present in the file, discards the match.

rules.title: Dynamic code evaluation (eval / new Function)
rules.description: Code built at runtime with eval or new Function executes with the full privileges of the process. If any part of the string can be influenced by a user, it becomes remote code execution.
rules.recommendation: Remove eval. Parse data with JSON.parse or use a lookup table of allowed operations.
remediation: Trace where the evaluated string comes from.
Replace eval/new Function with JSON.parse, a switch over allowed values or a safe expression library.
Add a Content-Security-Policy without 'unsafe-eval' in browsers.

rules.title: Shell command built from a template or concatenation
rules.description: child_process.exec runs the string through a shell. Interpolating variables lets an attacker append extra commands with characters like ; | && or $().
rules.recommendation: Use execFile/spawn with an argument array and no shell, and validate inputs against an allow-list.
remediation: Switch to execFile(cmd, [arg1, arg2]) or spawn(cmd, args, { shell: false }).
Validate every argument with an allow-list (e.g. /^[a-z0-9-]+$/).
Never pass request data straight to a shell.

rules.title: Child process started with shell: true
rules.description: With shell: true the arguments are interpreted by a shell, so metacharacters in user input become commands.
rules.recommendation: Remove shell: true and pass arguments as an array.
remediation: Set shell: false (the default) and pass arguments as an array.
Validate inputs with an allow-list.

rules.title: SQL query built with string interpolation
rules.description: Interpolating values into SQL lets an attacker change the query: read other users' data, bypass logins or modify tables.
rules.recommendation: Use parameterized queries or the ORM query builder.
remediation: Use placeholders: db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1', [id]).
With Prisma use $queryRaw`...${id}` (tagged template) instead of $queryRawUnsafe.
Validate types (numbers, enums) before they reach the query.

rules.title: Prisma $queryRawUnsafe / $executeRawUnsafe
rules.description: The Unsafe variants do not parameterize values. Any user input concatenated into them is SQL injection.
rules.recommendation: Use the tagged-template $queryRaw / $executeRaw, which parameterize automatically.
remediation: Replace with prisma.$queryRaw`SELECT ... WHERE id = ${id}`.
If dynamic identifiers are needed, choose them from an allow-list with Prisma.sql / Prisma.raw.

rules.title: MongoDB query built directly from request data
rules.description: Passing request objects as filters lets attackers send operators such as {"$ne": null} or {"$gt": ""} and bypass checks.
rules.recommendation: Build the filter from validated, typed fields and strip keys starting with $.
remediation: Pick fields explicitly: { email: String(req.body.email) }.
Validate the body with a schema (zod, joi) or use mongo-sanitize / Mongoose sanitizeFilter.

rules.title: dangerouslySetInnerHTML without visible sanitization
rules.description: React escapes output by default; dangerouslySetInnerHTML turns that off. If the HTML contains user content, it is stored or reflected XSS.
rules.recommendation: Render text normally or sanitize the HTML with DOMPurify before injecting it.
remediation: Prefer rendering plain text or Markdown with a safe renderer.
If HTML is required: DOMPurify.sanitize(html) on the server or client.
Add a strict Content-Security-Policy.

rules.title: Assignment to innerHTML / outerHTML / document.write
rules.description: These DOM sinks parse strings as HTML. Untrusted values here execute scripts in the victim's browser.
rules.recommendation: Use textContent / createElement, or sanitize with DOMPurify.
remediation: Replace el.innerHTML = value with el.textContent = value when no markup is needed.
Sanitize unavoidable HTML with DOMPurify.
Enable Trusted Types / CSP where possible.

rules.title: v-html / {@html} renders raw HTML
rules.description: v-html (Vue) and {@html} (Svelte) bypass template escaping. With user content this is XSS.
rules.recommendation: Use text interpolation or sanitize the HTML first.
remediation: Use {{ value }} / {value} for text.
Sanitize HTML with DOMPurify before binding.

rules.title: Outgoing request to a URL taken from the request
rules.description: If users choose the URL your server fetches, they can reach internal services, cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254) or localhost admin panels.
rules.recommendation: Only fetch URLs from an allow-list of hosts and block private IP ranges after DNS resolution.
remediation: Parse the URL, require https and check the hostname against an allow-list.
Resolve DNS and reject private, loopback and link-local addresses.
Disable redirects or re-validate each redirect target.

rules.title: Redirect to a user-supplied URL
rules.description: Unvalidated redirects are used in phishing: a link on your domain sends the victim to an attacker's site, and they can leak OAuth codes.
rules.recommendation: Only redirect to relative paths or to an allow-list of destinations.
remediation: Accept only paths starting with a single '/' (not '//').
Map short keys to fixed URLs instead of accepting full URLs.

rules.title: File system access with a path from the request
rules.description: Paths like ../../.env let attackers read or overwrite files outside the intended folder.
rules.recommendation: Resolve the path, then check it stays inside the allowed base directory.
remediation: const p = path.resolve(BASE, name); if (!p.startsWith(BASE + path.sep)) reject.
Prefer IDs mapped to files over raw file names.

rules.title: TLS certificate verification disabled
rules.description: Without certificate validation, anyone on the network path can impersonate the remote server and read or alter the traffic.
rules.recommendation: Keep verification on; add the internal CA with the ca option if needed.
remediation: Remove rejectUnauthorized: false.
For self-signed internal services, pin or add the CA certificate instead.

rules.title: JWT accepted with the 'none' algorithm or without expiry checks
rules.description: Accepting alg 'none' or ignoring expiration lets forged or stolen tokens authenticate.
rules.recommendation: Pin the expected algorithm and keep expiration checks.
remediation: jwt.verify(token, key, { algorithms: ['HS256'] }) (or your real algorithm).
Never set ignoreExpiration: true in production.

rules.title: Math.random() used for tokens or secrets
rules.description: Math.random() is predictable. Tokens generated with it can be guessed.
rules.recommendation: Use crypto.randomBytes / crypto.randomUUID / crypto.getRandomValues.
remediation: Replace with crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex') or crypto.randomUUID().

rules.title: MD5 or SHA-1 hashing
rules.description: MD5 and SHA-1 are broken for collision resistance and far too fast for passwords. Fine for non-security checksums, wrong for passwords or signatures.
rules.recommendation: Use SHA-256 for integrity and bcrypt/argon2/scrypt for passwords.
remediation: If this hashes passwords, migrate to argon2id or bcrypt.
If it signs data, use HMAC-SHA-256.

rules.title: Cookie configured without httpOnly or secure
rules.description: Session cookies without httpOnly can be stolen by any XSS; without secure they travel over plain HTTP.
rules.recommendation: Set httpOnly: true, secure: true and sameSite: 'lax' (or 'strict') for session cookies.
remediation: cookie: { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: 'lax' }.
If secure:false is only for local development, gate it on NODE_ENV.

rules.title: CORS reflects any origin while allowing credentials
rules.description: Allowing every origin together with credentials lets any website make authenticated requests as your logged-in users and read the responses.
rules.recommendation: List the exact origins that may call the API.
remediation: cors({ origin: ['https://your-site.com'], credentials: true }).
Never combine origin: true / '*' with credentials.

rules.title: Unsafe deserialization library
rules.description: node-serialize evaluates functions embedded in the payload; deserializing attacker data executes code.
rules.recommendation: Use JSON.parse with schema validation.
remediation: Remove node-serialize.
Validate parsed JSON with zod/joi.

rules.title: Next.js image optimization allows SVG
rules.description: Serving user-controlled SVG through the image optimizer can lead to XSS, and SVG processing was the vector of CVE-2026-96889 (fixed in Next.js 15.5.28 / 16.4.1).
rules.recommendation: Disable dangerouslyAllowSVG unless you need it; if you do, set contentDispositionType: 'attachment' and a strict contentSecurityPolicy.
remediation: Remove dangerouslyAllowSVG or pair it with contentSecurityPolicy: "default-src 'self'; script-src 'none'; sandbox;".
Keep Next.js and sharp updated.

rules.title: SQL query built with PHP variables
rules.description: Concatenating or interpolating variables into SQL lets attackers rewrite the query.
rules.recommendation: Use prepared statements (PDO/mysqli) or Eloquent/Query Builder bindings.
remediation: $stmt = $pdo->prepare('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?'); $stmt->execute([$id]);
In Laravel: DB::select('... where id = ?', [$id]) or ->whereRaw('id = ?', [$id]).
Cast numeric inputs with (int).

rules.title: Shell command executed with a PHP variable
rules.description: Variables in shell commands let attackers inject additional commands and run them on your server.
rules.recommendation: Avoid the shell; if unavoidable, escape each argument with escapeshellarg and validate with an allow-list.
remediation: Use a PHP library instead of calling a binary when possible.
Wrap every argument with escapeshellarg() and validate its format.
In Laravel use Process::run([...]) with an argument array.

rules.title: eval / assert / create_function / preg_replace /e
rules.description: Evaluating strings as PHP code is remote code execution if the string is attacker-influenced.
rules.recommendation: Remove dynamic evaluation; use explicit logic or preg_replace_callback.
remediation: Replace eval with a whitelist of operations.
Use preg_replace_callback instead of the /e modifier.

rules.title: include/require with a request parameter
rules.description: Including a file chosen by the user allows reading local files and, with log poisoning or uploads, executing code.
rules.recommendation: Map allowed page names to fixed files.
remediation: $pages = ['home' => 'home.php']; include $pages[$_GET['p']] ?? 'home.php';
Set allow_url_include=Off.

rules.title: Request data echoed without escaping
rules.description: Printing request values straight into HTML lets attackers inject scripts through a crafted link.
rules.recommendation: Escape on output with htmlspecialchars($v, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8') (or e() in Laravel, esc_html() in WordPress).
remediation: echo htmlspecialchars($_GET['q'] ?? '', ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8');
Use a template engine with auto-escaping (Blade {{ }}, Twig).

rules.title: Blade unescaped output {!! !!}
rules.description: {!! !!} prints raw HTML. With user-controlled content this is stored XSS.
rules.recommendation: Use {{ }} (escaped) or sanitize the HTML before printing.
remediation: Replace {!! $x !!} with {{ $x }}.
If HTML is required, sanitize it with a purifier (e.g. mews/purifier).

rules.title: unserialize() on untrusted data
rules.description: unserialize on attacker data enables PHP object injection, which with framework gadget chains leads to code execution.
rules.recommendation: Use json_decode, or unserialize($x, ['allowed_classes' => false]).
remediation: Store structured data as JSON.
If unserialize is unavoidable, pass ['allowed_classes' => false].

rules.title: Server-side request to a URL from the request
rules.description: Letting users choose the URL your server requests exposes internal services and cloud metadata.
rules.recommendation: Validate the URL against an allow-list of hosts and block private ranges.
remediation: parse_url() the input, require https and an allowed host.
Resolve DNS and reject private/loopback IPs; disable redirects (CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION false).

rules.title: File function with a path from the request
rules.description: User-controlled paths allow ../ traversal to read .env, config files or overwrite code.
rules.recommendation: Use basename() plus realpath() checks against a base directory, or map IDs to files.
remediation: $p = realpath(BASE.'/'.basename($name)); if (!$p || !str_starts_with($p, BASE)) abort.
Serve downloads by database ID instead of file name.

rules.title: Password hashed with md5/sha1
rules.description: Fast hashes are cracked in seconds with GPUs once the database leaks.
rules.recommendation: Use password_hash() / password_verify() (bcrypt or argon2id).
remediation: $hash = password_hash($password, PASSWORD_DEFAULT);
Rehash on next login with password_needs_rehash().

rules.title: extract() on request data
rules.description: extract() turns request keys into local variables, letting attackers overwrite variables such as $is_admin.
rules.recommendation: Read the specific keys you need.
remediation: Replace extract($_POST) with explicit $name = $_POST['name'] ?? ''.

rules.title: Mass assignment wide open
rules.description: With $guarded = [] or $request->all(), users can set columns you did not intend, like is_admin or user_id.
rules.recommendation: Use $fillable and $request->validated() / $request->only([...]).
remediation: Define protected $fillable = ['name', 'email'];
Model::create($request->validated());

rules.title: SQL built with f-strings, % or + in Python
rules.description: Formatting values into SQL strings allows injection; the driver cannot tell data from code.
rules.recommendation: Pass parameters separately: cursor.execute('... WHERE id = %s', (id,)).
remediation: Use driver placeholders (%s, ?, :name) with a parameters tuple/dict.
In Django use the ORM or params= in raw().
In SQLAlchemy use text('... :id').bindparams(id=id).

rules.title: os.system / os.popen / subprocess with shell=True
rules.description: Commands run through a shell interpret metacharacters, so variables become injectable commands.
rules.recommendation: Use subprocess.run([...], shell=False) with an argument list and validate inputs.
remediation: subprocess.run(['convert', src, dst], check=True)
Use shlex.quote only as a last resort.

rules.title: eval / exec on non-literal input
rules.description: eval/exec run arbitrary Python. With user input this is remote code execution.
rules.recommendation: Use ast.literal_eval for literals or explicit parsing.
remediation: Replace eval(x) with ast.literal_eval(x) or json.loads(x).

rules.title: pickle / marshal / unsafe YAML loading
rules.description: pickle and unsafe YAML execute code while loading. Never load them from users, cookies, caches shared with users or uploaded files.
rules.recommendation: Use JSON, or yaml.safe_load.
remediation: Replace yaml.load(x) with yaml.safe_load(x).
Replace pickle with json for data that crosses a trust boundary; sign it with HMAC if it must round-trip.

rules.title: HTTP request to a URL from the request (Python)
rules.description: User-chosen URLs let attackers make your server call internal services or cloud metadata.
rules.recommendation: Validate scheme and host against an allow-list and block private IP ranges.
remediation: urlparse() the input and check hostname in ALLOWED_HOSTS.
Resolve and reject private/loopback addresses; disable redirects.

rules.title: TLS verification disabled (verify=False)
rules.description: Disabling certificate checks allows man-in-the-middle attacks.
rules.recommendation: Remove verify=False; point verify= to a CA bundle for internal services.
remediation: requests.get(url) (default verify=True) or verify='/path/ca.pem'.

rules.title: Flask/Werkzeug debug mode enabled in code
rules.description: The Werkzeug debugger allows executing Python from the browser if it is reachable in production.
rules.recommendation: Drive debug from an environment variable that is off in production.
remediation: app.run(debug=os.environ.get('FLASK_DEBUG') == '1')
Serve production with gunicorn/uwsgi, never app.run.

rules.title: @csrf_exempt view
rules.description: Exempted views accept cross-site POSTs. Acceptable for signed webhooks, dangerous for session-authenticated actions.
rules.recommendation: Keep CSRF protection unless the endpoint authenticates each request in another way (signature, token).
remediation: Remove @csrf_exempt, or verify a webhook signature inside the view.

rules.title: Autoescape disabled / mark_safe / |safe
rules.description: Marking content as safe disables HTML escaping. With user data this is XSS.
rules.recommendation: Keep autoescape on and sanitize HTML (e.g. with nh3/bleach) before marking it safe.
remediation: Remove |safe / mark_safe for user content.
Sanitize allowed HTML with nh3.clean().

rules.title: random module used for secrets
rules.description: The random module is not cryptographically secure.
rules.recommendation: Use the secrets module.
remediation: secrets.token_urlsafe(32) / secrets.choice(...)

rules.title: JDBC/JPA query built with concatenation
rules.description: String concatenation in SQL/JPQL allows injection.
rules.recommendation: Use PreparedStatement placeholders or named parameters.
remediation: ps = conn.prepareStatement("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?"); ps.setLong(1, id);
In JPA: query.setParameter("id", id).

rules.title: Runtime.exec / ProcessBuilder with concatenated input
rules.description: Concatenated command strings or sh -c allow attackers to inject extra commands.
rules.recommendation: Pass a fixed executable and separate, validated arguments.
remediation: new ProcessBuilder("convert", src, dst) without sh -c.
Validate arguments with an allow-list.

rules.title: Java native or polymorphic deserialization
rules.description: Deserializing untrusted bytes with gadget-rich classpaths leads to remote code execution.
rules.recommendation: Use JSON with explicit types, or an ObjectInputFilter allow-list.
remediation: Replace native serialization with JSON DTOs.
If unavoidable, set ObjectInputFilter.Config.createFilter("com.example.*;!*").

rules.title: XML parser without XXE protection
rules.description: Default XML parsers resolve external entities, allowing file disclosure and SSRF through crafted XML.
rules.recommendation: Disable DOCTYPE declarations / external entities on the factory.
remediation: dbf.setFeature("http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl", true);

rules.title: Spring Security CSRF disabled
rules.description: Disabling CSRF is fine for stateless token APIs but dangerous for cookie-session applications.
rules.recommendation: Keep CSRF enabled for any endpoint authenticated by cookies.
remediation: Remove .csrf().disable() or scope it to stateless API paths only.

rules.title: Go SQL built with fmt.Sprintf or +
rules.description: Formatting values into SQL allows injection.
rules.recommendation: Use placeholders ($1 / ?) with arguments.
remediation: db.Query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1", id)

rules.title: InsecureSkipVerify: true
rules.description: Skipping certificate verification enables man-in-the-middle attacks.
rules.recommendation: Remove it and configure RootCAs for internal certificates.
remediation: tls.Config{RootCAs: pool}

rules.title: ActiveRecord query with string interpolation
rules.description: Interpolating into ActiveRecord SQL fragments allows injection.
rules.recommendation: Use hash conditions or placeholders: where('id = ?', id).
remediation: User.where(id: params[:id])
User.where('name = ?', params[:name])

rules.title: html_safe / raw on possibly user content
rules.description: html_safe and raw disable Rails escaping.
rules.recommendation: Use sanitize() with an allow-list or plain output.
remediation: <%= sanitize @post.body, tags: %w(p a strong em) %>
